title: After a host restart every execution that was running is recorded as a host restart, whatever order its end is processed in: a terminal server is gone when the one that ran the execution is gone, not when none answers at the moment the end is read
prompt:
Read crates/spawn-cli/src/recover.rs (the recovery: `interrupt_end`, `Facts::terminal_server_gone`, `classify`, the `host_restart` evidence in `end_evidence`, and the module comment), crates/spawn-core/src/port.rs (`TerminalHost::server_alive` and its comment: how a host restart is told from one terminal that vanished), crates/spawn-host/src/tmux.rs (`server_alive`: `list-sessions`, which never starts a server; `gone`; how each terminal and the fleet's runners are asked), crates/spawn-core/src/bridge.rs (`not_running`: an execution whose runner is gone ends `lost`; a terminal call that fails says nothing and leaves the execution as it is), crates/spawn-host/src/process.rs and the start-time reading in tmux.rs (`start_time`: a process told by its pid and its start time, not by its pid alone), and rsi/scenarios/028.sh's (8) (the host restart as the recovery's objective checks it).

The problem. After a host restart every execution that was running died with the terminal server, and each is to be recorded `execution.interrupted` cause `host_restart` (evidence `terminal_server: gone`), path `resume`. The recovery decides `terminal_server_gone` when it processes an end, from whether some terminal server answers at that moment (`!self.terminals.server_alive()`). The first resume after the restart starts a new terminal server. An end processed after that reads the new server as alive, and the execution is recorded cause `crashed` instead of `host_restart`. Which executions are recorded `host_restart` and which `crashed` depends on the order the Bridge sees and the recovery processes their ends: a resident seen one pass after five workers, whose resumes had started the new server, was recorded `crashed` (028 (8), journey j07, one run in four).

Required behaviour. (a) An execution's terminal server is gone when the server that ran it is gone: no terminal server answers, or the one that answers is not the one that ran the execution, as its start after the execution's start shows (a server and an execution are told apart as a process is: by when it started, not by whether something answers now). Mind the order of a start: the Bridge records an execution before it starts its terminal (bridge.rs `launch_and_prompt`), and that terminal's start may be what starts the server, so the server that ran an execution can be younger than the execution's record by the whole launch, which on a loaded host takes seconds. So the server that ran an execution is told by its identity taken when the execution's terminal started (or compared with an event recorded after that start), never by a comparison with the execution's record time, with or without a margin. The decision holds whatever order the ends are processed in, and whatever started a new server in between (a resume, another execution's start). (b) A server that answers and ran the execution is not gone: an engine killed while the server that ran it goes on is recorded `crashed`, never `host_restart`, also after a restart, for an execution started on the new server. (c) A host that cannot tell when its server started keeps today's rule (`server_alive` alone): an execution then reads as crashed, never as a host restart it cannot show. (d) Nothing else changes: the evidence of `host_restart` (terminal_server `gone`, loop_started_at_ms, boot_id, earlier_boot_id), its path `resume`, the revival keyed `recover-<execution>-<attempt>`, and every other cause's precedence and path stay as they are.

The gate judges this with rsi/scenarios/044.sh (read its header): a real `spawn loop` on a fake engine runs two workers, `first` and `second`; the loop is stopped as systemd stops it, the terminal server is killed with both engines, and the loop starts again 2 s later. Spawn's tmux (SPAWN_TMUX_PROGRAM, a wrapper) answers with an error for `second`'s terminal and for `list-panes -a` until `first`'s resume has started a new server, so `second`'s end is processed after a new server answers, every run. (1) `first`: `host_restart`, terminal_server gone, path `resume`, its resume by key, working again in its own native session with every line; (2) once the hold is lifted, `second`: the same; (3) `first`'s resumed engine killed (SIGKILL) while the new server runs: `crashed`, path `resume`, not `host_restart`, working again (the wrapper makes the `new-session` that starts that server wait 3.5 s, so the server is younger than the resumed execution's record by more than 2 s); (4) no work lost. It fails at (2) on the live main (afbde256): `second`'s end is recorded `crashed` (its terminal gone, no exit status), not `host_restart`. rsi/scenarios/028.sh must stay green.

What it saves. After a reboot the owner reads one cause for every agent that was running, the true one, and the recovery takes the host restart's path for each: a dashboard, an alert or a count of crashes no longer counts a reboot's survivors as crashes, at random, by the order a loop happened to see them.

Rules: never edit the protected paths, which the gate rejects: rsi/, scripts/ (scripts/rsi/, scripts/blackbox/, scripts/e2e.sh among them), deploy/, all of web/ except web/src/ and web/index.html, rust-toolchain files and .cargo/. The gate also rejects fewer runnable tests than the base, any lint relaxation and any build-time code. The gate builds offline from the cargo caches already on the host. Keep every existing check green and add tests of your own for the new behaviour.
